When node.arg is not in self._protected and not yet in self._rename_map, allocate a new generic name via self._next_name() and store the mapping under node.arg in self._rename_map.

When node.arg is not in self._protected, mutate node.arg to self._rename_map[node.arg] (using the freshly allocated mapping if one was just inserted) and return the node so the renamed declaration is emitted in ast.unparse output.

spec.implementation_notes:
Mirror the structure of the existing visit_Name method on _VariableAnonymizer (harness/cross_examiner.py:108-116). The new visit_arg should: (1) early-return node if node.arg in self._protected, (2) if node.arg not in self._rename_map, insert self._rename_map[node.arg] = self._next_name(), (3) assign node.arg = self._rename_map[node.arg], (4) return node. Do not call generic_visit on the ast.arg (it has no relevant children to traverse for renaming). Do not add new state to __init__ and do not alter _collect_protected or _collect_params. For tests, use ast.parse + ast.unparse round-trips or direct substring assertions on anonymize_code output: feed code like 'def f(x):
    def g(y):
        return y + 1
    return g(x)' and assert that the inner parameter and its body reference are both rewritten to the same var_N token, while x remains x.

spec.implementation_notes: By overriding visit_arg, we intercept ast.arg nodes. Since _collect_protected collects top-level arguments, they are in self._protected and will be skipped. Nested and lambda arguments are not top-level, so they are not in self._protected. Renaming them and adding them to self._rename_map ensures that subsequent Name node visits (which reference these parameters) will look up the same renamed mapping and be consistently anonymized.
